svg.text: Turning an idea I find into a tested strategy
Not every idea is my own. When I see something interesting, I put it through the same pipeline. Worked example: a public VIX-reversal study.
1 · The study I came across — research by others, not mine
QQQ — forward returns after the biggest intraday VIX drops
SPY — the same signal on the broad index
On the days the VIX falls hardest intraday,
forward equity returns skew strongly positive
Interesting enough to test. Step one is to
rebuild it myself and distrust it until the
Source: public research found online (dates, VIX open-price drop, and 30-day / 90-day / 1-year forward returns). Shown as the raw claim — before any verification of mine.
2 · How I turn it into research → backtest → strategy

text.tspan: — an interesting result in someone else's research — like the tables above.
— pull the raw data and reproduce the study myself; distrust it until it replicates exactly.
— re-run it on other markets and vary the parameters/thresholds — a real edge survives, a fitted one doesn't.
— this study has no buy/sell rules or stops, so I define automatic detection, entry/exit and risk management.
— stands on its own → a strategy; if not (drawdown, inconsistency, too few trades) → a regime filter that sharpens other strategies.

svg.text: Idea → verification → stress-test → a strategy, or a regime filter. This one is at step one: spotted, not yet verified.
